Some schools have missing or null values in the School Name column, which can cause issues when filtering or grouping by school name.
The Provision Type column in the school nutrition table is mostly null (82%), so queries filtering on provision type may miss many schools.
The Excellence Rate columns in the school performance table have many null values (26%), which can skew averages or cause missing results.
The Power column in the cards table uses '*' to represent no power, and also has nulls; queries must handle both cases.
The Language column in the card foreign printing table has values like 'Portuguese (Brazil)' but queries may use 'Portuguese (Brasil)' or 'Portuguese', causing mismatches.
The Legality Status column has values 'Legal', 'Banned', 'Restricted' but case may vary; queries using 'legal' may miss 'Legal'.
The Month column in the monthly account statement table is stored as text in YYYYMM format, so date functions may not work directly.
The Average Monthly Balance can be negative, which may affect calculations like averages or sums if not handled.
The Weight column in the superhero table uses 0 to indicate missing weight data, which can be mistaken for a real weight of zero.
Loan status codes are not self-explanatory; 'C' means running/ok, other codes mean defaulted or finished, so filtering on status must use the code.
Race lap time is stored as text in some tables and as integer milliseconds in others, so numeric comparisons need conversion.
Driver nationality and constructor nationality use different value sets; 'Japanese' appears in both but counts differ.
Event date is stored as text with time component, so YEAR() extraction requires string parsing.
Member IDs appear in multiple formats across tables (text rec-style vs integer), so joins on member may fail.
Circuit country values are inconsistent (e.g., 'Germany' vs 'German'), so country filters may miss rows.
Qualifying rank column is stored as time text, not numeric rank, so ranking comparisons need parsing.
Many driver birth dates are null, so youngest/oldest queries may exclude drivers.
Many school-level attributes (provision type, funding model, charter number) are mostly NULL, so filtering on them silently drops most schools.
School IDs are stored as text and differ in format between tb001/tb003 and tb002, so joins on School ID can fail or mismatch.
Excellence Rate columns in tb002 are largely NULL, so averages/ratios over them cover only a subset of schools.
Card data is spread across multiple printings per Oracle ID; counting rows in tb004 counts printings, not unique cards, so distinct Oracle ID must be used for card counts.
Power/toughness are stored as text and use '*' for variable values, so numeric comparisons on cl0143/cl0157 fail or exclude those cards.
Legality status is per format; a card can be legal in one format and banned in another, so 'banned' must always be qualified by format.
Many card attributes (flavor text, keywords, EDHRec rank) are NULL for a large share of printings, so filters on them undercount.
Account and client IDs in the banking tables are not consistent across tables (tb013 uses Account ID/Client ID ranges that differ from tb015/tb017), so joins can lose rows.
Transaction amounts in tb022 can be negative and direction is encoded separately, so summing cl0236 without filtering direction gives wrong totals.
Race results are split across tb028/tb030/tb031/tb032/tb035 with overlapping Race IDs and different row grains, so joining them without dedup double-counts points.
Lap times are stored as text (e.g. '1:40.006'), so AVG/MIN on them requires parsing to seconds first.
Superhero weight uses 0 to mean missing, so AVG(weight) or weight filters must exclude 0.
Patient lab values use '+'/'-' text codes and normal ranges differ per test, so numeric comparisons must apply test-specific thresholds.
